dietEvidence.body: The dentition is consistent with herbivory. No gut contents are known, and the plants eaten and feeding height are inferred from tooth shape and neck anatomy.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: A dicraeosaurid with extremely long, forward-curving neural spines on the neck. The spines are bone; their display or defensive role is inferred.
summary: Bajadasaurus pronuspinax is a dicraeosaurid sauropod from the Bajada Colorada Formation of Argentina. It is known from a partial skull and skeleton, including extremely long cervical neural spines that curve forward. The spine function—display, defence or both—remains unresolved.

discovery.body: Named by Gallina et al., 2019. The record is known from Bajada Colorada Formation, Neuquén. A partial skull and skeleton with well-preserved cervical spines.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: Bajada Colorada Formation, Neuquén records the species in the Early Cretaceous. The numeric range used here is ≈140–134 Ma, an occurrence estimate rather than a direct date on every specimen.

fossilEvidence.title: Cervical spine series
fossilEvidence.body: The holotype preserves a partial skull and skeleton, including the elongated cervical neural spines. The spines are bone; the soft tissue that covered them is not preserved.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The cervical neural spines are long and curved forward, and the neck is relatively short.

behaviour.body: The forward-curving neck spines are unusual and may have supported display structures or defensive spines. Neither function is demonstrated. Social behaviour and parental care are unknown.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from a partial skull and skeleton with well-preserved cervical spines. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: The material is incomplete and the sample is small. The elongated spines are direct evidence, but their soft-tissue covering and function are inferred. No gut contents or behaviour traces are known.
